sections.title: Headline
sections.content: AI-agent infrastructure dominates this week's GitHub attention: coding-agent skills, context management, worktree orchestration, and agent-facing internet access occupy much of the top tier. A second cluster applies the same agent/RAG trend to code review, knowledge management, and geospatial visualization.

sections.title: bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view
sections.description: A browser-based spy-satellite simulator built around real data and a photorealistic 3D globe.

sections.title: alibaba/open-code-review
sections.description: A hybrid deterministic-plus-LLM code-review system with line-level comments and multilingual security rules.

sections.title: ayghri/i-have-adhd
sections.description: An agent skill designed to keep coding-agent output concise and answer-focused.

sections.title: affaan-m/ECC
sections.description: An agent-harness optimization system covering skills, memory, security, and research-first development.

sections.title: stablyai/orca
sections.description: An application development environment for running fleets of parallel coding agents across desktop, mobile, and remote runtimes.

sections.title: Tencent/WeKnora
sections.description: An open-source LLM knowledge platform combining document RAG, autonomous reasoning, and a self-maintaining wiki.

sections.title: obra/superpowers
sections.description: An agentic skills framework and software-development methodology.

sections.title: Panniantong/Agent-Reach
sections.description: A CLI that gives agents access to major social, video, code, and web sources without paid APIs.

sections.title: blader/humanizer

sections.title: addyosmani/agent-skills
sections.description: Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Coding-agent infrastructure dominates: ECC, superpowers, agent-skills, context management, worktree management, and parallel-agent runtimes. Agent-enabled code review, RAG knowledge systems, and broad web retrieval form adjacent clusters. Among the ten selected repositories, Python and JavaScript each appear three times, TypeScript twice, Go twice, and Rust and Shell once each.

sections.title: Notable Shifts
sections.content: The center of gravity is moving from standalone model wrappers to agent operating infrastructure: reusable skills, constrained context, persistent memory, safe parallelism, and access to real software and information systems. The strong performance of gods-eye-view also shows that distinctive visual applications remain capable of breakout attention.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: This week's signal is less about a new model and more about making agents dependable inside real workflows. The opportunity is shifting toward the surrounding runtime and experience layer, while novel visual products remain a viable source of breakout interest.
